newsitem.title: JAPAN: US, Japan to discuss insurance spat in Washington.
newsitem.headline: US, Japan to discuss insurance spat in Washington.

text.p: Finance Minister Wataru Kubo and U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky will meet soon to try to resolve a bilateral dispute over deregulation of Japan's insurance market, officials said on Wednesday.
"It's an important meeting which will be taken seriously by both sides," U.S. ambassador Walter Mondale said after a meeting with Kubo.

The dispute centres on U.S. allegations that Tokyo is poised to renege on a 1994 insurance trade pact by opening up its so-called "third-sector" niche market before substantially deregulating primary life and non-life insurance business, where domestic firms hold sway.
Foreign firms have a strong foothold in the third sector, which includes cover such as personal accident and health care.

A Japanese ministry official said Kubo and Mondale had agreed that the talks on the insurance dispute were proceeding, but that gaps remained. They also agreed to work towards taking the discussions further, he said.

The official said it could be difficult for Kubo and Barshefsky, who will meet in Washington, to have substantive talks as Kubo's schedule was tight. At the moment there were no working-level talks scheduled in Washington, he said.

Mondale said Kubo and Barshefsky would meet on the sidelines of a gathering of the Group of Seven (G7) industralised countries on Saturday. G7 finance ministers and central bankers will be in Washington for the annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank, which run until October 3.
Japan and the United States have already failed to meet a July 31 deadline for resolving the insurance dispute, and working-level talks last week left the two sides far apart.

On Tuesday, U.S. President Bill Clinton, in a meeting with Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto in New York, urged mutual efforts to resolve a dispute over implementation of the 1994 pact, as well as a dispute over aviation.
